set.body:
Scope:
Correct scala-slurm's planning boundary so scheduler-affecting resources and placement cannot live outside the managed canonical request.

Target flow:
JobIntent[A] -> SiteProfile.resolve -> ResolvedJobRequest[A] -> staging/canonicalization -> ManagedController -> Scheduler.

Acceptance criteria:
- JobIntent carries ResourceRequest and SiteIntent with explicit requested semantics.
- SiteProfile resolution produces a typed ResolvedJobRequest containing the concrete EffectiveSiteSpec and requested provenance.
- Managed canonicalization, digest conflict detection, codecs, local CLI, SSH agent protocol, and replay operate on the resolved concrete request.
- Retries and recovery replay recorded effective allocation and cannot re-evaluate changed defaults silently.
- A changed resource or placement plan under the same submission key yields a typed digest conflict.
- Preflight policy rejection remains distinct from scheduler rejection and controller authority remains explicit/advisory.
- Canonical JSON golden fixtures cover absent defaults, memory modes, accounts, partitions, QoS, constraints, modules, containers, accelerators, environment export, and allowed native options.
- CLI and SSH conformance tests prove equivalent concrete requests and exact arguments.
- Repository-wide scala-slurm compile/test/format/package gates pass.
set.title: SOJ.R2: Make requested and resolved Slurm plans durable
